packageRules.description: Crates: Cargo.lock within the caret ranges, or a range in Cargo.toml when a release falls outside it, both cargo roots, one pull request, with major updates in a pull request of their own beside it (separateMajorMinor). Held for dashboard approval while :dependencyDashboardApproval is in extends; a vulnerability-fix pull request skips that approval.

Remote actions, SHA and version comment together, one pull request, with major updates in a pull request of their own beside it (separateMajorMinor). Held for dashboard approval while :dependencyDashboardApproval is in extends; a vulnerability-fix pull request skips that approval.

The toolchain in four places, every one read from the same tags of the rust image on Docker Hub, the -slim-bookworm variant the Dockerfile builds on: channel in rust-toolchain.toml, rust-version in Cargo.toml, fuzz/Cargo.toml and loadgen/Cargo.toml, and the Dockerfile's build stage. The two regex managers keep only -slim-bookworm tags through extractVersionTemplate, and docker versioning keeps the Dockerfile on its suffix, so no member moves to a release whose image is not on Docker Hub; this is the tag-set option, not a minimumReleaseAge. Docker versioning keeps the component count: channel and the Dockerfile tag read x.y.z-slim-bookworm and move on a patch, rust-version reads x.y-slim-bookworm and moves only on a minor; the official image pushes both tags from one build. A digest-only Dockerfile update, when the image is rebuilt under the same tag, moves only the digest, which is harmless. Held for dashboard approval, because a toolchain moves the clippy lint set; a vulnerability-fix pull request skips that approval.
The distroless run stage: a digest under the nonroot tag. Held for dashboard approval; a vulnerability-fix pull request skips that approval.

Tool pins in pyproject.toml; the hosted app relocks pixi.lock on the same branch, and a stale pixi.lock fails lock-check. Held for dashboard approval; a vulnerability-fix pull request skips that approval.

requires-python in pyproject.toml, the one thing the pep621 manager reads there. pixi owns Python through python = "3.14.*", so the floor moves by hand with that pin. The pixi manager's reading is its own and stays on.

nextest-version in .config/nextest.toml equals the cargo-nextest pin in pyproject.toml, so both read conda-forge and move in one pull request. Held for dashboard approval; a vulnerability-fix pull request skips that approval.
The tooling package's release tag, which also moves the allium pin. Held for dashboard approval; a vulnerability-fix pull request skips that approval.
pixi itself: the requires-pixi floor in pyproject.toml and pixi-version in the setup action, one pull request. Held for dashboard approval; a vulnerability-fix pull request skips that approval.
The github-actions manager would read setup-pixi's pixi-version input under prefix-dev/pixi as well; the regex manager owns it.
Lock-file maintenance rewrites pixi.lock and tools/quint/package-lock.json as well as Cargo.lock. Held for dashboard approval; a vulnerability-fix pull request skips that approval.

Binaries in tools.txt and source builds in tools-source.txt. Each is a download nothing verifies beyond the transport or the registry checksum, and rustqual is a gate. Held for dashboard approval; a vulnerability-fix pull request skips that approval.

The Quint CLI in tools/quint/package.json, pinned exactly, and package-lock.json relocked with it on the same branch; a stale lock fails lock-check. Quint pins the evaluator it downloads on first use, so moving it moves that too. It also names the Apalache version it expects, which tools/quint/apalache.txt pins by SHA-256 and Renovate does not track: lock-check fails until that file's quint= names the new version, set after reading the new CLI's DEFAULT_APALACHE_VERSION_TAG and moving apalache= and sha256= if it moved (docs/how-to/maintain-dependencies.md, decision 0021). Held for dashboard approval; a vulnerability-fix pull request skips that approval.
Hook revs in both prek configs, one pull request, because a hook is code the gate runs on every commit. Held for dashboard approval; a vulnerability-fix pull request skips that approval.
lychee moves by hand: LYCHEE_VERSION in both argument lists must match its rev, and its tag prefix is lychee-v.

customManagers.description: rust-toolchain.toml's channel, from the rust image's x.y.z-slim-bookworm tags (see the rust toolchain rule).
rust-version in the workspace, fuzz and loadgen manifests, the channel's major.minor, from the rust image's x.y-slim-bookworm tags (see the rust toolchain rule).
tools.txt and tools-source.txt: one name@version per line, resolved on crates.io.
nextest-version, which must equal the cargo-nextest pin in pyproject.toml, read from the same conda-forge package.
requires-pixi, the floor that moves with pixi-version in the setup action.
setup-pixi's pixi-version input, read here rather than by the github-actions manager, under the requires-pixi floor's depName.
Hook revs in both prek configs: a full SHA with the release tag as its comment. lychee's lychee-v comment does not match.
